keyVerseText: And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following. Amen.
rootMeaning: The word πανταχοῦ (pantachoû) is derived from the genitive case of a presumed derivative of πᾶς (pâs), which means 'all' or 'every.' As an adverb of place, πανταχοῦ literally conveys the sense of 'in all places' or 'universally.' This root meaning goes beyond the simple English gloss of 'everywhere' by emphasizing the totality and comprehensiveness of the location or extent, implying no place is excluded.
usageInScripture: πανταχοῦ occurs seven times in the New Testament and is consistently translated to convey the idea of 'everywhere' or 'in all places,' with five instances simply as 'every where.' Other translations include 'men every where' and 'in all places,' showing that the word can apply broadly to spatial presence or the reach of people. This consistency highlights the word's function to denote universal scope or presence without limitation.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, the universal scope embedded in πανταχοῦ underscores the global nature of the Gospel message and God's work through Christ. It reminds believers that the power and presence of God are not confined to any one location but extend to all corners of the earth. This universality reflects the Great Commission's call to preach to all nations and the inclusiveness of God's kingdom. Understanding this word helps believers appreciate the all-encompassing reach of divine activity and the call to participate in that expansive mission.
keyVerseReflection: In Mark 16:20, the phrase 'preached every where' uses πανταχοῦ to emphasize the comprehensive spread of the apostles' preaching. It conveys that the message of Christ was not limited to a single region but went out to all places, with the Lord actively working alongside them and confirming their message through signs. This word enriches the verse by highlighting the unstoppable and universal advance of the Gospel through the early church.
